learning: Race 10 is the best measured design (830.86). Its slalom line loss of 0.85 is below the 1.0 threshold, so the geometry is kept. Each further change this iteration would be untested on the final robot, so the controller and geometry are held to race 10 values.
notes: Race 10 platform and controller reproduced exactly, with no change to geometry or gains. Slalom line loss of 0.85 and 9/20 finishes are the reference for the final unseen-track race.
rationale: Race 10 (score 830.86) is the best measured robot. Its geometry is exactly the Builder's proposal: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 with y = 0.06, body 0.12 m by 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg. Its controller is kp 3.2, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 0.95, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], line_loss last_direction. Oval finished 20/20 and s-bend 20/20. Slalom finished 9/20, with line loss down to 0.85, under the 1.0 threshold I set for keeping the geometry. Race 9 showed that wheel_track 0.10 m loses slalom finishes, and the revert is already accepted. Race 3 (widening to 0.04 m) and race 6 (seven sensors) both failed. Mass 0.6 kg is untested, and this is the final iteration with no later race to correct a new platform, so I do not change geometry. For the controller, the race 10 settings produced the best measured score, and every change I could make is untested on this geometry, so I keep the controller identical to race 10. Expected result, not measured: the same platform should repeat close to race 10, with the slalom finish rate the main source of variance.
